feed.title: NPR Topics: Science
feed.subtitle: The latest health and science news. Updates on medicine, healthy living, nutrition, drugs, diet, and advances in science and technology. Subscribe to the Health & Science podcast.

entry.title: This summer was hot. August shattered global heat records
entry.summary: Scientists say that August was the hottest month ever recorded globally. In the U.S., summer temperatures also shattered heat records.

entry.title: A fossil feather from the age of dinosaurs may explain why only some birds survived
entry.summary: An extremely well preserved fossil feather could reveal why some birds survived the dinosaur-killing asteroid, and others did not.

entry.title: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
entry.summary: The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.

entry.title: Are we any closer to detecting dark matter?
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with theoretical astrophysicist Priyamvada Natarajan of Yale University about a strange blip recorded by a dark matter detector in South Dakota and what the fluke could mean.

entry.title: 'Her body temperature was 106': How heat is killing Americans in their homes
entry.summary: Heat kills thousands of people across the U.S. every year. The risk is especially high for the millions of Americans who live in manufactured housing like mobile homes and trailers.

entry.title: From bottles to bakery: How scientists create edible cookies from recycled plastic
entry.summary: New research at the American Chemical Society meeting showcased a potentially edible cookie made out of — plastic!

entry.title: Biologist Andrew Newhouse on the genetic revival of the American chestnut
entry.summary: The American chestnut once dominated the Eastern woodlands. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Andrew Newhouse, an environmental biologist, about efforts to bring these trees back from the brink of extinction.

entry.title: This week in science: Archaeology fakes, hurricanes and lizards, and heat health effects
entry.summary: NPR's Regina Barber and Nate Rott talk about a new way to spot archaeological fakes, how hurricanes may have influenced lizard evolution and the health effects of extreme heat.

entry.title: Scientists map key protein interactions linked with profound autism
entry.summary: Research published in the journal Science illuminates a "missing piece" in the biological understanding of profound autism and offers new targets for drug development.

entry.title: Scientists study how the brain of a fish filters out signals
entry.summary: The elephantnose fish is native to Africa and a darling of neuroscientists, for its specialized cerebellum-like brain. Scientists have mapped the neurons in a part of the brain that senses electrical signals in detail, and found that how it filters out electrical noise is more complex than they thought.
